signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: CHF/JPY is under significant pressure as JPY marks a dominant +1.594% average weekly outperformance across the G10, while CHF lags at -0.711%. The resulting 2.304% G10 spread establishes a critical bilateral theme driven by a shift in safe-haven preferences and a -100bp carry disadvantage for CHF (SNB 0.0% vs BoJ 1.0%). While JPY COT LF net short remains large at -124,575, the JPY Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +22.9 supports the currency's recovery against a weak CHF backdrop. JPY real rates at -0.70% remain less accommodative than NZD or CHF, further supporting the JPY bid in a consolidating market. Risk-off flows are clearly favoring JPY over CHF as the MOVE index retreats to 80.5. Risk: A sharp spike in the VIX above 25 that triggers a broader CHF safe-haven catch-up trade.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Options + Vol
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.87, testing the SMA200 at 157.97 after a sustained move below its SMA20/50 cluster. The options market signals aggressive downside hedging with a 25d Risk Reversal of -3.19, a strong put skew that aligns with a negative Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of -1.1% (IV 7.2% vs HV30 8.3%). This negative VRP suggests the market is underpricing potential realized volatility despite the pair's 1.44% weekly decline. While a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%) structurally supports the pair, the heavy LF spec short of -124,575 is vulnerable to further deleveraging if 157.00 fails. Risk: Intervention threats or a hawkish shift at the next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) accelerate the spec short squeeze.

signals.title: NZD/USD — RBNZ + COT Positioning
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5871, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5803/0.5792/0.5827) as markets position for upcoming Q2 jobs data. Despite an RBNZ hiking stance (2.5% rate) and a strong positive ESI of +33.4, COT LF positioning remains net short -30,606 with an extreme long% of only 9.7%. This heavy spec short positioning contrasts with the RBNZ's tightening bias and recent 3.12% monthly gain, creating a high-conviction short-squeeze setup if employment data confirms the need for further hikes. The carry deficit of 125bp against the USD remains the primary headwind for long extensions. Risk: Q2 jobs data misses expectations, validating the crowded spec short and breaking the SMA cluster support.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Premium + Technicals
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3441, maintaining a position above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3396/1.3364/1.34). The options market is pricing a massive volatility premium with a VRP of +4.8%, as ATM IV of 11.0% significantly exceeds realized HV30 of 6.2%. This elevated premium suggests heavy institutional hedging ahead of US Non-Farm Payrolls, despite a neutral 0bp carry differential (Fed 3.75% vs BoE 3.75%). COT data shows specs are already net long +36,661 (67.3% long), suggesting the trend is well-understood but expensive to protect. Risk: A hawkish Fed surprise at the next meeting on 16 Sep that collapses the GBP/USD technical floor.

signals.title: NZD/CHF — Retail Divergence Extreme
signals.text: NZD/CHF retail sentiment has reached an extreme 85% short reading, directly fading the pair's 3.12% monthly appreciation in the underlying NZD/USD cross. This retail extreme develops while the NZD ESI remains strongly positive at +33.4, suggesting retail traders are prematurely fading institutional momentum driven by RBNZ hiking expectations. With a +250bp carry premium favoring NZD (RBNZ 2.5% vs SNB 0.0%), the cost of carry further penalizes the retail short position. This divergence typically precedes a 'stop-out' rally as retail capitulates. Risk: A broader shift to risk-off sentiment (VIX > 25) that triggers a safe-haven CHF bid, validating the retail short bias.
